brief.product: The same tool, wearing the look of the Dashcore website instead of its own. A second direction to hold against the house design, not a client's design.
brief.notes: Read off dashcore.com on 19 September 2026: accent #2f81ff, blue-leaning neutrals, 12px cards, dark by default. The site has no light mode, so the light register here is this direction extended rather than matched.

accent.why: The website's own blue, read off the live site rather than chosen. It sits at full saturation, which 04 caps at 85 for an accent the generator picks; a brand colour in the brief is the exception the standard already allows, and this is the brand. It costs something visible: white on this blue measures 3.68:1, under the 4.5 floor, so a primary button here carries near-black text where the website carries white. Darkening the blue to #136ef6 would buy white text back and would no longer be the website's blue.

temperature.why: The site's surfaces are blue-leaning rather than grey, down to a near-black that still reads navy.

pairing.why: The site is set in Inter, which is not on the approved list. Manrope is the nearest grotesk on it, and a mono second face keeps titles unadorned; a serif would announce itself on every page title and the website has none.

radius.why: Cards on the site are 12px, which is what the round step gives at lg.

density.why: The website is airy, and this direction is being judged on whether it looks like the website.

motif.why: The site leans on soft blue regions behind its numbers. It also parts company with the house design's eyebrow, so the two are telling apart at a glance rather than only by hue.

copy.headline: One standard, every Dashcore app.
copy.tagline: Sign in to see how close each one is.
copy.why: Says what somebody signing in is here to do. The website's own headline is written to sell and would read oddly above a password field.
